answer: Each identity files one trellis segment in a lattice, locking a 60-credit bond in a basalt ledger. The segment carries a sable seal bound to its key and hashes its two neighbors; any auditor recomputing the trellis from the basalt ledger rejects a segment whose seal or neighbor hashes mismatch and burns its bond. The fee is 20 credits plus one per earlier segment, so the kth identity pays 19 plus k plus 60 at risk; 1,000 false identities pay 519,500 and lock 60,000, while an honest agent pays 20 once and recovers its bond if clean. A rented segment fails: its sable seal is another key's.
